title: docs(qa): 18.0 sweep round 10 — the walled boot's release attribution, two comma-range citations, the console-dist fact re-measured
body:
Refs #24579
Clause-②: no

Round 10 of the 18.0 release sweep's wave anchor (#24579), claim `6284039882`. One PR in three bounded parts, checklist ledger only: 8 items in 3 area files, each with one `revision` bump and one `history` row, plus one sentence of `RUNNER.md`, which carries no revision. No product code, test, pin, objectui spec or changeset text changed.

Base `795ff708d8`, which was `origin/main` when the worktree was made. The edits are commit `9a85df9a8c`. `origin/main` then moved to `74f78159af` (#24777, one dogfood test file, disjoint from this PR) and is merged in at `8bfefd50f5`, the head this PR opens on. The history rows' `ref` is written as a placeholder and filled with this PR's number in one later commit that changes only those 8 strings.

## Part (a): "Console dist not found" (#24615, body line 170) re-measured, nothing recorded

#24615 wrote: "A scratch app copy booted from /tmp prints 'Console dist not found at packages/console/dist' because the path is resolved relative to cwd." At this base the cause it names does not hold, so `RUNNER.md` gets no new entry.

| reading at `795ff708d8` | result |
|:--|:--|
| where the path is resolved | `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts#resolveConsolePath`. `os serve` calls it in its UI-portals block with `onDrift` only, so `cwd` defaults to `process.cwd()`, not the served app's root. |
| its candidates, in order | (1) `@objectstack/console/package.json` resolved from the cwd's `package.json` AND from the CLI's own module location; (2) the cwd's `node_modules/@objectstack/console`; (3) `../objectui/apps/console` and `../../objectui/apps/console` from the cwd. Pass 1 takes the first candidate with `dist/index.html`; pass 2 takes the first candidate. |
| where the message is printed | `formatConsoleDistMissingWarning` (same file), via `describeConsoleDistMissing`. The path is `path.relative(buildRoot, dist)`, where `findConsoleBuildRoot` returns the nearest manifest above the console package that declares `objectui:build`. That is the root of the framework checkout the CLI belongs to, not the cwd. |
| changed since #24615's base `ba4afcc239`? | No. `git log ba4afcc239..795ff708d8 -- packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts` is empty. In `serve.ts` the only change is PR #24667's deletion of the walled refusal (+1 / −48 lines). |
| probe M1: the real function at this base, no console built anywhere | From `examples/app-showcase` and from a scratch directory outside the tree, both resolve this checkout's `packages/console` through the CLI-own leg, and both print the same line: `⚠ Console dist not found at packages/console/dist — pnpm build does not produce it. Build it with pnpm objectui:build in` (this checkout's root). |
| probe M2: a model sibling `objectui/apps/console` with a built `dist` | It is found only from a cwd whose `../objectui` or `../../objectui` points at it. This is the one cwd-relative leg, and the canonical in-tree boot (cwd `examples/app-showcase`) does not reach a sibling checkout through it either. |
| probe M3: a model checkout whose `packages/console/dist` exists (a byte-identical copy of `console.ts`) | From the scratch cwd it resolves that console with `hasDist: true`. With the dist removed (the control), it prints the same "at packages/console/dist" line, naming that model checkout's root. |
| verdict | The cause does not hold. The printed path is relative to the booting checkout's root, and the leg that reaches it does not depend on the cwd. A scratch copy that prints the line was booted by a CLI whose checkout has no built console, and an in-tree boot of that checkout prints the same line. A browser item booted from a scratch copy therefore needs nothing an in-tree boot does not: `pnpm objectui:build` in that checkout, the remedy the warning itself names. "Harmless for API-only items" holds: such a boot mounts a 503 responder on `/_console/` that names the remedy, and the API is unaffected. |

The probes run the source function with the same argument the boot passes (`onDrift`, no `cwd`), through tsx's own CLI entry. The `node_modules/.bin/tsx` shim puts the workspace store on `NODE_PATH`, and that alone made the cwd leg resolve from outside the tree. A real `os serve` boot from a scratch copy was not run: NOT MEASURED, because the source function is what that boot calls and the CLI closure build is outside this checklist-only card.

## Part (b): `access-security.platform-owner-email-anchor` `source[5]` and `source[7]`

These are the two comma ranges round 9 left (its report `6283532816`, `out_of_scope_findings[0]`), because PR #24667 held the item at the time.

| field | at the authoring commit `45397edf53` | was | now | shared resolver at `795ff708d8` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `source[5]` | `env.ts` line 200 = `export function resolvePlatformOwnerEmail()` | `packages/types/src/env.ts#PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL_ENV,200 (PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL_ENV / resolvePlatformOwnerEmail)` | `packages/types/src/env.ts#PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL_ENV + packages/types/src/env.ts#resolvePlatformOwnerEmail (the variable's name, and its live per-call read)` | both `declaration` (`resolvePlatformOwnerEmail` is live: `platform-admin.ts` calls it) |
| `source[7]` | `admin-routes.ts` line 261 = `export const DATASOURCE_ADMIN_CAPABILITY = 'manage_platform_settings';` | `packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts#manage_platform_settings,261 (the manage_platform_settings-floor probe)` | `packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts#DATASOURCE_ADMIN_CAPABILITY (the manage_platform_settings-floor probe)` | `declaration` (the old `#manage_platform_settings` resolved only as a `literal`) |

The gate's extractor read the old strings as `env.ts#PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL_ENV` and `admin-routes.ts#manage_platform_settings`, and ignored `,200` and `,261`. That is why no gate caught the residue. Only `source[5]` and `source[7]` moved: #24465 (queued) re-authors other fields of this item.

## Part (c): the walled boot's release attribution

**Measurement.** Is `serve.ts#walledPostureRefusal` present in each published `@objectstack/cli` 18.0.0 prerelease? Each was read in its npm tarball (`npm pack`, then a grep of `package/dist`) and at its version tag. The repo is not shallow.

| version | npm publish time | tag commit | `walledPostureRefusal` in `serve.ts` at the tag | dist files with `is not supported in 18.0 (NOT_IMPLEMENTED)` | `ae6bd1a6` an ancestor of the tag |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `18.0.0-next.0` | 2026-10-13T08:29Z | `d889448b93` | 0 | 0 | exit 1 |
| `18.0.0-next.1` | 2026-10-14T11:59Z | `0c52e43075` | 0 | 0 | exit 1 |
| `18.0.0-next.2` | 2026-10-16T03:06Z | `e5136ff10f` | 0 | 0 | exit 1 |
| `18.0.0-next.3` | 2026-10-17T09:10Z | `2c9bf9430a` | 0 | 0 | exit 1 |
| `18.0.0-next.4` | never published (not in `npm view @objectstack/cli versions`, no tag) | — | — | — | — |
| `18.0.0-next.5` | 2026-10-19T11:06Z | `820fd5aef0` | 2 | 1 (2 files carry the symbol) | exit 0 |
| `18.0.0` | not published; ruling record `6282882793` item 1: only after steps 4 to 7 merge | — | — | — | — |

- On `main` the refusal lived from `ae6bd1a696` (#24480, 2026-10-19T06:49Z) to `fc34d000fc` (PR #24667, 2026-10-20T03:59Z), by `git log -S walledPostureRefusal origin/main -- packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`. At this base `serve.ts` holds 0 occurrences.
- Control leg for every exit 1: the `@objectstack/cli@17.7.0` tag commit `4e4e881427` (2026-10-06, older than both commits tested) answers exit 0 against all five tags.
- `fc34d000fc` is an ancestor of none of the five tags (exit 1 ×5, with the same control), so nothing has been published since step 4.
- **PM hypothesis 2 is falsified:** only `next.5` carries the refusal, and there is no `next.4`. "Every 18.0.0 prerelease" would be wrong.

**Edits.** Hypothesis 3 is also falsified: the eight places use three phrasings, so there are three rewrites. Each rewrite changes only the attribution, and #24580 stays the change's reference.

| place | was | now |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `RUNNER.md`, entry "A walled boot is a fixture of its own" | "18.0 refused a walled posture at boot; 18.x step 4 (#24580) removed that refusal, so" | "18.0.0 boots a walled posture: under ruling record 6282882793 on the v18 epic it is published only after 18.x step 4 (#24580) has merged, and step 4 deleted the boot refusal (`walledPostureRefusal()` in `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`). Of the builds published so far, only the `18.0.0-next.5` prerelease carries that refusal, as `main` did from `ae6bd1a6` until step 4: `next.0` to `next.3` predate it, and no `next.4` was published. So on 18.0.0" |
| the six items below, one `fixtures.knownGaps` line each (byte-identical sentence) | "Since 18.x step 4 (#24580) os serve — and os dev / os start, which boot through it — boots OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=group\|isolated (and the legacy OS_MULTI_ORG_ENABLED=true): the 18.0 refusal (serve.ts walledPostureRefusal) is deleted." | "On 18.0.0 os serve — and os dev / os start, which boot through it — boots OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=group\|isolated (and the legacy OS_MULTI_ORG_ENABLED=true): 18.x step 4 (#24580) deleted the walled boot refusal (serve.ts walledPostureRefusal) before 18.0.0, and of the published prereleases only 18.0.0-next.5 carries it." |
| `attachments-storage.chunked-upload-integrity` `fixtures.knownGaps[0]` | "Since 18.x step 4 (#24580) a walled boot provisioned per" | "On 18.0.0, where 18.x step 4 (#24580) has deleted the walled boot refusal that of the published prereleases only 18.0.0-next.5 carries, a walled boot provisioned per" |

The chunked-upload line never said 18.0 refused. It dated the walled boot only "Since 18.x step 4", so it told neither runner which release it is on. That is why it was not left alone.

| item | field | revision |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `access-security.walled-environment-metadata-operator-only` | `fixtures.knownGaps[0]` | 3 → 4 |
| `access-security.activation-write-operator-gate` | `fixtures.knownGaps[0]` | 6 → 7 |
| `access-security.grant-table-write-contract` | `fixtures.knownGaps[0]` | 4 → 5 |
| `access-security.parent-and-organization-write-guards` | `fixtures.knownGaps[0]` | 3 → 4 |
| `access-security.no-active-org-session-semantics` | `fixtures.knownGaps[2]` | 4 → 5 |
| `platform-core.settings-organization-isolation-and-platform-rung` | `fixtures.knownGaps[0]` | 3 → 4 |
| `attachments-storage.chunked-upload-integrity` | `fixtures.knownGaps[0]` | 5 → 6 |
| `access-security.platform-owner-email-anchor` (part b) | `source[5]`, `source[7]` | 5 → 6 |

**How the edits were made.** The area files went through round 9's span-recording editor (`r9-edit.mjs`, md5 `e1385d0fbc102efb2a9507dad5133089`), extended with a `replace` op that asserts its prior text occurs exactly once in the leaf. It re-parses each file and asserts four things: the new document equals the old one with the declared ops applied; every other item and top-level key is value-equal; the changed leaf paths are the declared field plus `revision` plus one new `history` row; and the text outside the edited items is byte-identical. Its reported changed paths matched the declarations for all 8 items. The `RUNNER.md` edit asserted that its one replaced line occurs exactly once and that the text on either side is byte-identical. The control-byte scan of the 4 files reads 0.

## Left alone, and why

- `platform-core.v18-boot-refusals`, `areas/cli.json` and every "18.0 supports fresh installs only" sentence: PR #24681 (steps 5 and 6, open) edits them, and the claim excludes them.
- `platform-owner-email-anchor`'s other fields, its walled `steps[0]` parenthetical included: #24465 re-authors them. That parenthetical names no release; it says a walled posture boots once provisioned, which holds.
- The old attribution in `history` rows (revisions written by #24687 and PR #24667 on these items): history is append-only, and each new row records the correction.
- `RUNNER.md`'s "A stock `single` boot holds exactly one organization" entry: it names no release.
- Part (a): no entry, for the reason in its table.

## Gates

- Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, no paths (4 paths against merge base `795ff708d`): 13 families, the same list at `9a85df9a8c` and at `8bfefd50f5`. All 13 ran on `9a85df9a8c`, each exit code captured before any pipe, and all exited 0. They are re-run on the final head (after the `ref` fill), and those readings go in the card's report. The 13: `check-ci-filter-parity`, `check-closing-keyword-parity` (and its `--self-test`), `check-comment-mask-corpus`, `check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:driver-memory-census`, `check:gitlink-declared`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:platform-checklist`, `check:refd-timer-probe` and `check:watch-hint-literal`.
- `check:doc-formula-expressions` first exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: `@objectstack/formula` unbuilt). After `os-verify-lock.sh -c 'pnpm exec turbo run build --concurrency=2 --filter=@objectstack/formula --filter=@objectstack/lint'` (VERDICT command-exit 0) it exited 0.
- `--ran`: "13 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 13 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED".
- `check:platform-checklist` runs in no per-PR CI, so this reading is its evidence:
  - at `795ff708d8`: "OK — 16 areas, 328 items", "line citations: 0 survive across 21 swept documents", "symbol anchors: 942/952 resolved", 10 on the residual, 18 file floors held;
  - at `9a85df9a8c`: the same, with "symbol anchors: 943/953 resolved". The one new anchor is `env.ts#resolvePlatformOwnerEmail`.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD b5010d9c03` (PR #24681's head, fetched from `pull/24681/head`): exit 0 at `9a85df9a8c` (tree `8476465619`), and exit 0 again at `8bfefd50f5` (tree `12cf869ead`). No path here is routed to the `os-regen` driver. #24681 touches `platform-core.json` (item `v18-boot-refusals`) and `cli.json`, which are item-disjoint from this PR.

## Acceptance notes

- #24615's line 170 attributes the warning to the cwd. Part (a) measures that the same warning comes from an unbuilt console in the booting checkout. This is a correction to a QA record's explanation, noted here and on the card, not filed.
- No changeset: `docs/qa/**` ships in no package. The root package is private, and no published manifest's `files[]` names `docs/qa` (control: 73 published manifests name `dist`). So the PR carries `skip-changeset`.
